u/aaronC is correct on his advice, but forgot to include how essential elemental orbs to mid and late game combat. You need to set these on enemies for massive damage during chain attacks and to continue the chain.

Setting an orb is a matter of doing three stages of a blade combo. It can be as easy as spamming spinning edge for three light orbs, or choosing another blade. CPUs will try switching to help continue the combo, or you can make them start one. The final special in a combo decides the orb set. You can only set one orb or each element at a time, so synergy in your blade elements is vital for stacking. Also, setting an orb elemental already on an enemy overrides the last seal in effect.

In chain combos, the goal is to break the orbs you set for additional turns and increase the damage multiplier. To burst an elemental orb you need to hit it with 3 attacks; an attack of an opposite element (EX hitting a Fire orb with a Water attack, a Dark orb with a Light attack) will count as 2 hits instead of just 1. If you use a blade with the opposite element, that attack will prioritize hitting the orb it deals extra damage to. If you use a blade that does not have any element advantage, it will prioritize hitting an orb that only needs 1 attack left to break, otherwise it'll choose at random.

Breaking five orbs in a chain attack will result in a full burst with the last used blade in a chain attack, while the others use driver combos.

Each elemental orb has their own effect. Sealing will make certain fights much easier, especially when the foe will prevent you from doing blade specials or driver arts.

Early game combat is honestly a tedious chore, since it's harder to recharge driver arts and build up specials quickly. Remember to stand next to your blade in combat to charge specials up quicker. Use driver arts during the last hit of your auto-attack string. Once cooldown happens after an auto-attack string, move a bit to reset the string and re-attack quicker. When you get the affinity skill that lets you chain driver arts into another, start timing special arts to hit immediately after a driver art, and time blade switching at the end of the special. You can also time a driver art after switching blades for a special gauge boost, too.

It's a lot to remember so I'll simplify the tips; Time your arts and blade switching, cancel auto-attack cooldown, CPUs will prioritize blade combos to set orbs for chain attacks over driver combos, and hit orbs in chains with an opposite element.
